title: Inspect and extend: History ordering and next-check time
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/exposure.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve tocheck, lastcheck, formatting, interval calculation, and empty state.
problem: A history list is a stack of dated events. Trace how a service response becomes a row, how newest checks are selected, and how a due timestamp is calculated. Notice that no history means “No check yet.”. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/exposure.ts` and the related project files: src/exposure.ts; src/screens/StatusScreen.tsx.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to tocheck, lastcheck, formatting, interval calculation, and empty state.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: The configured interval is a UI rule, not health guidance.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: A history list is a stack of dated events. Trace how a service response becomes a row, how newest checks are selected, and how a due timestamp is calculated. Notice that no history means “No check yet.”
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/exposure.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
